newsitem.title: Indonesia: Germany's Kohl invites E.Timor bishop to meeting.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl invites E.Timor bishop to meeting.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl has invited East Timorese Nobel Peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo for a meeting during his current visit to Jakarta, German delegation sources said on Monday.
It was not immediately known whether Belo had accepted the invitation. There was no answer at his home in the East Timor capital Dili and his church aides were not immediately available for comment.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee early this month awarded the peace prize jointly to Belo and to self-exiled East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta for their efforts towards securing a peaceful solution to the issue of East Timor.
Indonesian President Suharto met Belo during a recent visit to East Timor but made no mention of the award to the bishop.
Kohl arrived in Indonesia on Saturday and spent Sunday relaxing and fishing with Suharto in the Java Sea north of Jakarta.
He had further talks on Monday with Suharto during the formal part of his visit. He is due to leave for the Philippines on Tuesday morning.
Indonesians have generally acknowledged Belo as a worthy recipient of the peace prize but have been bitterly critical of the award to Ramos-Horta.
Ramos-Horta has called on Kohl to raise the issue of East Timor with Suharto during his visit to Jakarta and seek a withdrawal of Indonesian troops from the former Portuguese colony.
During his visit to Suharto's Merdeka (Freedom) Palace on Monday, Kohl received an honorary membership to the Indonesian Engineers' Association.
During a speech marking the occasion, the German leader referred to the need to respect human rights.
"Respecting the rights of man and human rights is central to the future...this question should be raised openly among friends," Kohl said.
Indonesian troops invaded East Timor in December 1975 and Jakarta declared the territory its 27th province the following July in a move never recognised by the United Nations.
